title: Biological approach: the brain
summary: Localization of function, how brain imaging techniques work, and how experience reshapes the brain through neuroplasticity.

keyterms.definition: The idea that specific brain areas are responsible for specific functions, such as Broca's area for speech production.
A region of the left frontal lobe involved in speech production; damage causes difficulty producing fluent speech.
A medial temporal lobe structure involved in forming new long-term (declarative) memories and spatial navigation.
Magnetic resonance imaging: produces detailed images of brain structure.
Functional MRI: measures changes in blood oxygenation to show which brain areas are more active during a task.
Electroencephalography: electrodes on the scalp record electrical activity; excellent timing but poor spatial detail.
Positron emission tomography: tracks a radioactive tracer to show brain activity; invasive and slow.
The brain's ability to change its structure and function in response to experience, learning or injury.
The removal of rarely used synaptic connections, making neural networks more efficient.
A group of interconnected neurons that fire together; repeated activation strengthens the connections.
Studying animals to test biological hypotheses that would be unethical or impossible in humans; raises generalization and ethical issues.

questions.prompt: Scoville and Milner (1957) described patient HM after removal of parts of both medial temporal lobes. What was the main result?
options: He lost all memories from childhood
He could no longer form new long-term declarative memories
He lost his short-term memory completely
questions.explanation: HM had severe anterograde amnesia but intact short-term memory, supporting the role of the hippocampus in forming new long-term memories.

questions.prompt: Broca's patient "Tan" (1861) understood speech but could barely speak. Post-mortem damage was found in the:
questions.explanation: This supported the localization of speech production to Broca's area in the left frontal lobe.

questions.statement: HM could still learn new motor skills, such as mirror drawing, even though he did not remember practising.
questions.explanation: Procedural memory relies on different structures, showing that memory types are localized differently.

questions.statement: fMRI directly measures the firing of individual neurons.
questions.explanation: fMRI measures blood oxygenation (the BOLD signal), an indirect marker of neural activity.

questions.text: Maguire et al. (2000) used ___ to compare the hippocampi of London taxi drivers with controls.
questions.explanation: Structural MRI showed taxi drivers had larger posterior hippocampi.

questions.text: The imaging technique with the best temporal resolution (timing) is ___.
questions.explanation: EEG records electrical activity in milliseconds, but cannot locate activity precisely.

questions.prompt: Match each technique to what it shows best.

pairs.right: Activity during a task via blood oxygen

questions.explanation: Choosing a technique is a measurement decision: each has strengths and limits.

questions.prompt: Which is a limitation of using brain imaging to study localization?
options: Activity in an area shows correlation with a task, not that the area alone causes the behaviour
It cannot show any brain structures
questions.explanation: Many areas are active in any task, and imaging is correlational, so causal claims are limited.

questions.prompt: Why might case studies of brain damage, like HM, be hard to generalize?
options: Damage is unique to the individual and the brain may have changed before or after
questions.explanation: One person's damage and history are unique, so findings may not apply to everyone.

questions.prompt: Order these techniques from best to worst spatial resolution (roughly).
questions.explanation: Structural MRI shows fine detail; EEG records from the scalp and is poorest at locating activity.

questions.prompt: Maguire et al. (2000) found that taxi drivers' posterior hippocampal volume:
options: Correlated positively with years spent as a taxi driver
questions.explanation: The correlation with time driving suggests experience changed the brain, though the study was quasi-experimental.

questions.prompt: Draganski et al. (2004) taught participants to juggle for three months. What happened?
options: Grey matter in motion-processing areas increased, then decreased after they stopped
questions.explanation: This experiment shows learning-related plasticity and "use it or lose it".

questions.statement: Draganski et al. (2004) is stronger evidence for causation than Maguire et al. (2000) because the brain was scanned before and after learning.
questions.explanation: The pre–post design shows the change followed learning, whereas Maguire compared existing groups.

questions.statement: Synaptic pruning is a sign of brain damage.
questions.explanation: Pruning is a normal process that removes unused connections to make networks more efficient.

questions.text: Rosenzweig, Bennett and Diamond (1972) found rats raised in ___ environments developed a heavier cortex.
questions.explanation: Toys, companions and challenges stimulated cortical growth, an animal model of plasticity.

questions.text: "Neurons that fire together, wire together" describes how ___ networks are strengthened.
questions.explanation: Repeated co-activation strengthens synaptic connections (long-term potentiation).

questions.prompt: Match each study to its finding.

pairs.right: Larger posterior hippocampus in taxi drivers
Enriched rats had a heavier cortex
HM could not form new memories

questions.explanation: Three show plasticity; HM shows localization of memory.

questions.prompt: A limitation of generalizing Rosenzweig et al. (1972) to humans is that:
options: Rat brains and environments differ from humans'
questions.explanation: Animal research allows control and invasive measures, but species differences limit generalization.

questions.prompt: Which is a sample limitation of Maguire et al. (2000)?
options: Only 16 right-handed male taxi drivers were studied
questions.explanation: A small, all-male sample limits generalization.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of neuroplasticity during learning.
items: The same neurons are repeatedly activated together
Synaptic connections strengthen and networks form
questions.explanation: Practice strengthens used pathways while unused ones are pruned.
